newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorean activists protest Taiwan nuclear waste deal.
newsitem.headline: SKorean activists protest Taiwan nuclear waste deal.

text.p: South Korean environmental activists protesting Taiwan's contract to ship nuclear waste to North Korea demonstrated in front of the Taiwan mission in downtown Seoul on Thursday.

Women dressed in traditional Korean costumes waved pickets reading, "To survive, protect our land from nuclear waste," and resident foreigners holding laminated flags representing their home countries read statements in English and Japanese.

Taiwan and South Korea have been embroiled in a dispute sparked by a contract between Taiwan Power Co and a North Korean state firm to ship up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste to the Stalinist regime.
"We think this is an international crime," said Choi Kyung-song of the Korean Federation for Environmental Movement.
"Nuclear waste is dangerous and must not be sent to North Korea. We plan to block the shipment and we will expand on international solidarity."
Greenpeace confirmed its support and pledged to stop the shipment.
"We call on the governments of Taiwan and North Korea to cancel their agreements for nuclear waste shipment," said English teacher Jim Walsh, reading a Greenpeace statement to about 100 protesters.
"If they do not, all non-violent means of citizen intervention to prevent this dangerous plan will be undertaken."
South Korean organisers said similar protests were scheduled for nine cities in Asia, North America and Europe on Friday.

In New York, five lawmakers from Seoul visited the United Nations on Thursday to lobby against the deal. They said the shipment, if delivered, would make it difficult to approve funding for light-water nuclear reactors for North Korea.
Pyongyang will receive the new reactors from a consortium including the United States, Japan and South Korea in return for closing down its current reactors, which produce weapon-grade plutonium.
Seoul is footing the bill for most of the $4.5 billion project.
The row between South Korea and Taiwan heated up in January when Korean activists protesting in Taipei were beaten by Taiwanese nationalists and deported.
China has slammed Taiwan for the deal with North Korea.
Taiwan maintains the deal is strictly business and says the Taipei-Pyongyang waste pact complies with all international regulations and that shipments would be securely packed in steel barrels.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with either North Korea or South Korea, both of which recognise Taipei's rival -- the communist Chinese government in Beijing.
